newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs rise, await Fed rate decision.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs rise, await Fed rate decision.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were mostly higher in quiet trade on Tuesday as the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) met to consider an increase in U.S. interest rates.
Traders and analysts said ADR markets were likely to shrug off a rate hike. Many analysts expect the U.S. central bank to increase its federal funds rate to 5.5 from 5.25 percent.

Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan "has done a masterful job prepping everybody for the rise, and when it comes it will be a relief," said Francois Gour, Latin American equity strategist at Caspian Securities.
A trader said a rate rise "is a foregone conclusion. A quarter point is the target, and if they do nothing the market will probably sell off."
Brazilian telephone company Telebras rose 1/2 to 108 and Telefonos de Mexico fell 1/8 to 39-3/4. The companies were the most active ADRs in overall light trade.
Swedish telephone equipment company LM Ericsson rose 1/2 to 34-1/8. Finland's Nokia Group fell 1/8 to 59-3/4 after its chief executive said the company had a solid foundation for success.
Asked about a rate increase, analysts said a rise would strengthen the dollar against other currencies.

So foreign companies that have revenues in dollars or big U.S. sales, such as oil, drugs and telephone equipment firms, could be helped in particular, said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR sales and research at NatWest Securities.

A rate increase would have little effect on investors attracted to Latin American ADRs and local stocks by economic reforms, lower inflation, low valuations and the surge in local markets, analysts said.
Advancers led decliners by 263 to 200 among 806 ADRs in late morning. The ADR index rose 0.29 percent and volume was 23 million shares.
